Based on the reproducer and the two snippets, what’s happening is:

1. Your TileImage (XYZ) source is built with `url: "/…/{z}/{x}/{-y}.png"`, so its internal tile‐URL function knows how to invert y.
2. But your TileDebug source never gets that URL template (or the resulting `tileUrlFunction`), so it falls back to the default `{z}/{x}/{y}` URL logic—hence the debugging labels never show the inverted y.

The fix is to pass through the same `url`/`urls` (or even an already constructed `tileUrlFunction`) from the TileDebug options into the base XYZ constructor. That way, `getTileCoordForTileUrlFunction(...)` will correctly apply the `{-y}` inversion when drawing its debug labels.

Here is a single *SEARCH/REPLACE* patch in `src/ol/source/TileDebug.js` to carry the URL template and/or an existing `tileUrlFunction` through:

```javascript

      opaque: false,
```

With that change, when you do:

```js
new TileDebug({
  url: '/service@EPSG_3857/{z}/{x}/{-y}.png',
  /* … other XYZ opts … */
});
```

the debug layer will now use the same `{-y}` inversion logic and show the correct inverted‐Y coordinates in its labels.
